purpose: E167 raised the open-set diagnostic AUC to 0.7999 with E65+logbp feature concat but W stalled at 0.6997 because the fused Train-OOF quantile threshold drifts. E170 asks two questions: (1) does adding the E162 raw-EEG embedding as a third stream push the diagnostic AUC past 0.7999, and (2) with the scores frozen, how much W is reachable at all if the threshold is swept over 2000 quantiles (E159 style), and what diagnostic AUC would be required for W = 0.80.

logbp.note: 90-d log band power (5 bands x 18 channels)

standardisation.rule: per stream, task-wise z-score with Train-session1 statistics only (all Train rows of that task), identical to E143/E163/E167 so the E65 control reproduces 0.7578 / 0.6958 exactly

two_way_concat.note: control for E167; block_norm concat 64+32 -> PCA-96 k=6 should reproduce diagnostic AUC 0.7999

three_way_score.simplex_rule: all (w65, wlogbp, w162) on a 0.1 grid with sum = 1 (66 points, includes the three single-stream corners)
three_way_score.train_selected_rule: weight chosen by Train LOSO AUC of the fused score only; Test never consulted
three_way_score.z_normalisation: each stream score z-scored with its own 5-block Train OOF mean/std before weighting

ceiling.note: E159 method: sweep 2000 quantiles of the frozen score, for each threshold take Test S1 rejection / S2 acceptance directly and derive LOSO rejection from the Train-OOF acceptance rate implied by the same threshold (per-fold known-block quantile)

protocol.prototypes: k-means (E143 seeding, 20 iters) per (task, identity) on fit_rows only
protocol.train_oof: 5 contiguous frac blocks, prototypes rebuilt without the held block
protocol.threshold: quantile of the 5-block Train OOF score at each acceptance rate; LOSO uses the per-fold known-block quantile
protocol.test: scored only; session used only for the post-hoc diagnostic AUC

reporting.test_official: N/A: the Test split has no public labels; session labels are used only for the diagnostic AUC after scoring
